clue.text: Unhappy? In pieces, presumably!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be upset or distressed
second meaning: something ... has been chopped into bits

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'presumably' flag the second, literal reading: whatever is cut up should be in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal idiom for being distressed and also literally describes something chopped into portions.

clue.text: Brand about to be absorbed by companies, all limited, in recession

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside, so about goes within the companies

parts.note: CO is short for company, so two of them give two COs
CA is circa, about

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the trimmed word is turned round
limited means curtailed, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A business report: a brand taken over by limited companies during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL limited is AL, and 'in recession' turns that to LA.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft drink is one of the most recognised trade names in the world.

clue.text: This writer brought up to follow the Golden Rule?

indicators.note: to follow puts the writer's letters after the rest

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: brought up means raised; in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: this writer means the setter, me

explanation.surface: The writer was raised to obey the golden rule of treating others as yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold. The question mark marks the definition as loose: a theorem is a proved proposition, a kind of rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A proven mathematical statement is a general principle, a law that always holds.

clue.text: Way to get over cold detailed by dope causing disease?

parts.note: a path is a way
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
gen and dope both mean information

indicators.note: detailed means with the tail removed, so the last letter goes

parts.note: icy means cold

explanation.surface: Getting over a cold by taking drugs, and possibly falling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' is read as de-tailed, losing its tail; 'dope' is information, not a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Germs that produce illness are described with this adjective, which means producing sickness.

clue.text: This has plot penned by a woman

definitions.text: This has plot penned by a woman

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the plot sits inside the woman's letters

parts.note: a dame is a woman
a bed is a garden plot, as in a flower bed

explanation.surface: A self-description: this book has a storyline written by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the novel was written by George Eliot, the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, so a woman really did write its plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel is George Eliot's first full-length work, so its plot really was written by a female novelist.

clue.text: Rage in The Iliad distressed divinely comedic writer!

indicators.note: distressed means agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Anger in Homer's epic upset a great poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iliad opens with the rage of Achilles, a nice touch for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine poet wrote the Divine Comedy, so he is the writer of a divine comedy.

clue.text: Beverage that stimulates partner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the South American caffeinated herbal tea
second meaning: a companion or spouse

explanation.surface: A drink that gets your other half going.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the caffeine-rich infusion from Paraguay and a friend or spouse.

clue.text: Echo Spider-Woman dropping new complaint

parts.note: E is Echo in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so those letters fall out

parts.note: Arachne, in Greek myth, was turned into a spider

explanation.surface: A comic-book heroine called Echo loses a fresh complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Spider-Woman looks like the Marvel heroine, but here it is Arachne, the weaver Athena changed into a spider.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the ear is a minor ailment, and complaint is a common word for an illness.

clue.text: Ostentation came at first in story read the other way

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the turned story
reading the other way means the letters run backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: at first means only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: Showiness arrived early in a tale read backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE read the other way is ELAT; C from 'came' goes in it, with 'in' as the placing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan means brilliant display or showy success, close to flamboyance.

clue.text: White blokes in tussle when covering great crime movie

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the scrambled letters surround the great word
in a tussle things get scrambled, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: big means great

explanation.surface: White men scuffling over a serious offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' is not praise for the film but a synonym that the scrambled letters wrap around; 'crime movie' fits because the plot turns on a fake kidnapping.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coen brothers' 1998 comedy is built on a kidnapping and ransom plot, so it fits the crime genre.

clue.text: We hear adulterer spotted quick one!

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the answer sounds like the adulterer word

parts.note: an adulterer is someone who cheats on a partner, a cheater

explanation.surface: Gossip about a fast-moving unfaithful spouse who has been seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'seen', but it describes the animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat has a spotted coat and is the fastest land animal.

clue.text: Instinctive person sure to succeed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coming naturally, without learning
second meaning: someone with innate talent who is bound to do well

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for innate behaviour and a noun for someone with inborn ability.

clue.text: Really good cook's old bouncer retrained

indicators.note: something retrained is put through a new regime, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A former nightclub doorman has retrained as an excellent chef.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, from a ribbon once worn by knights, describes cooking or a chef of the highest class.

clue.text: Glaswegian companion leaving whisky?

indicators.note: the companion leaving means those letters depart from the whisky

parts.note: Scotch is whisky from Scotland
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A man from Glasgow whose drinking partner walks out on the whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the post-nominal letters of a Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Glasgow is an example of a native of Scotland.

clue.text: With spy boss, unsuccessfully watch online channel

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories
ill means badly, as in ill-judged
to stream is to watch video over the internet

explanation.surface: A spymaster fails to watch a TV channel online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like a TV station, but it is a watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrow flow of water that drives a mill wheel is a man-made water course.

clue.text: Swift traveller, bird lodged in shelter shortly before another tucked into meat

indicators.note: before places the first assembly ahead of the second
lodged in means housed within, so the bird goes inside
shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the shelter word is dropped

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
the emu is a large flightless bird

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the gull goes within the meat

parts.note: liver is offal eaten as meat
another bird: the gull

explanation.surface: A cryptic recipe: one bird nesting in a shelter, another stuffed inside some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like speed, but it is the satirist Jonathan Swift, whose traveller is the hero of his most famous book.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift's satirical novel follows the voyages of this ship's surgeon, his most famous character.

clue.text: People's Princess finally discharged so in the pink?

definitions.note: a noun naming the plant group; the definition is a whimsical description of its members

indicators.note: finally discharged means the last letter is let go

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, was called the People's Princess
thus means so

explanation.surface: Princess Diana was finally released, so she is in good health?
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' usually means healthy; here it means belonging to the pinks, the flowers of this genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus of flowering plants includes carnations and the garden pinks.

clue.text: Famous Italian goalie, agile, I'll foul

indicators.note: a foul is an illegal play, and foul also means to mess up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nimble keeper owns up to a foul in a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomer and physicist from Pisa is one of the best-known Italians in history.

clue.text: Ring round village for some old pagan worshippers?

definitions.text: Ring round village for some old pagan worshippers?

parts.words: Ring round village for some old pagan worshippers?
parts.note: a cryptic description of a Wiltshire settlement inside a vast prehistoric stone circle

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a sinister cult surrounding a village; in fact the village sits inside a Neolithic henge and stone circle in Wiltshire, a county of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wiltshire village lies within the largest Neolithic stone circle in Britain, thought to be a ritual site.

clue.text: French here succeeded in LA base, free from clerical status

indicators.note: in places the French word and S inside the other letters

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
ici is French for here
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A Frenchman reached Los Angeles and has left the priesthood.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the mathematical constant used as the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to secularise, to remove something or someone from church control.

clue.text: Cornish region not viewed in country paradise

indicators.note: not viewed in means unseen within, so those letters vanish from the country

parts.note: Sweden is a Scandinavian country
SW, the South-West, is the region of England that contains Cornwall

explanation.surface: A rural idyll where part of Cornwall cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: SW is the compass-style abbreviation for the South-West of England, home of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden is the archetype of a perfect place, a byword for bliss.

clue.text: Given relief since being trapped in rising river

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so since goes within the river
rising means going up; in a down clue the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
as means since, as in as it was late

explanation.surface: Rescue for someone stuck in a flooding river.
explanation.definitionFit: If pain or tension has been lessened, it has been soothed or alleviated.

clue.text: Amateur player from insanely rich nation

indicators.note: insanely means crazily, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A sportsman from an absurdly wealthy country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amateur' and 'rich' together suggest a gentleman sportsman, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: The term, from the Corinthian Casuals football club, means a sportsman who plays for love rather than pay.

clue.text: Tree bearing gift from Prometheus

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A tree carrying a present from a Greek god.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titan Prometheus stole flame from the gods and gave it to humanity.

clue.text: Whip suited Chief of Staff's offices in the House?

indicators.note: the chief of a word is its first letter
to whip is to beat or whisk, so the letters of suited are stirred up

explanation.surface: A party whip in Parliament dressed in a suit, and the chief of staff's rooms there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' and 'the House' suggest Parliament, but the house is any home and the whip is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms in a home set aside for work or reading serve as private offices.

clue.text: Chicken is served with rook hearts and wine

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook
a hen is a chicken
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A dinner menu: chicken served alongside rook hearts, with wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock and other white wines from the Rhine valley are traditionally called by this adjective used as a noun.

clue.text: Poet in some Hebridean island on time

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the island follows the time

parts.note: a day is a period of time
Lewis is the northern part of the Outer Hebridean island of Lewis and Harris

explanation.surface: A poet stays on a Scottish island for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' is fair because Lewis and Harris form one island, so Lewis is only part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Day-Lewis was Britain's Poet Laureate from 1968 to 1972.

clue.text: Judge returns lacking initial answers

indicators.note: returns means the remaining letters go back the way they came
lacking initial means the first letter is missing

parts.note: to esteem is to judge or consider

explanation.surface: A judge comes back without any first replies.
explanation.walkthrough: ESTEEM without its first letter is STEEM; 'returns' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a demand or a need is to satisfy or respond to it, as in meets the brief.
